newsitem.title: USA: Blues harmonica player William Clarke dies.
newsitem.headline: Blues harmonica player William Clarke dies.

text.p: Acclaimed blues harmonica player William Clarke has died in a California hospital after collapsing before a show, a spokesman for his record label said on Monday.

Clarke, 45, died of a bleeding ulcer on Saturday at a hospital in Fresno, Alligator Records spokesman Marc Lipkin said. He collapsed in his hotel room on Friday before a scheduled show in Fresno and was rushed to the hospital, Lipkin said.
Clarke, also a singer and songwriter, had just completed a six-week cross-country tour after releasing "The Hard Way", his ninth album.

Mixing Chicago blues traditions with West Coast swing in a combination called "soul-jazz," Clarke was regarded as one of America's leading blues harmonica players and his records won rave reviews from critics.
Clarke spent a week in the hospital last March after collapsing in Indianapolis. He found out he had congestive heart disease. He shed 60 pounds and returned to the club circuit a few months later.
Clarke had been a full-time blues musician since quitting his job as a machinist in 1987.
Born March 29, 1951, in Inglewood, California, Clarke fell in love with the blues through early Rolling Stones albums.

He befriended blues legends like T-Bone Walker, Eddie Vinson, Big Joe Turner and the man who was to become his mentor, George "Harmonica" Smith. The two worked together from 1977 until Smith's death in 1983.

Between 1978 and 1989, Clarke recorded and released five self-produced albums on shoestring budgets and guested on nearly a dozen other albums. While fame eluded him, he built an impressive word-of-mouth reputation, receiving six W.C. Handy nominations, the Grammy award of the blues community.

He won a W.C. Handy award in 1991 for Blues Song of the Year with his composition "Must be Jelly" from his Alligator debut album, "Blowin' Like Hell". That was followed by "Serious Intentions" in 1992 and "Groove Time" in 1994, which won him widespread critical acclaim.
Clarke is survived by his wife Jeannette, son William and daughter Gina.
